paper_information.title: A perspective on Integrated Disease Management Strategies in Minor Tropical Fruit Crops of India
paper_information.abstract_summary: This chapter describes the diseases, symptoms, and Integrated Disease Management (IDM) approaches for minor tropical fruit crops including watermelon, cucumber, sapota, and jamun. It emphasizes combining physical, cultural, biological, and chemical control measures to manage multiple diseases simultaneously while reducing environmental hazards and chemical resistance.
paper_information.research_objective: To review and describe the diseases, symptoms, and Integrated Disease Management (IDM) strategies for minor tropical fruit crops such as cucumber, watermelon, sapota, and jamun in India.
important_findings: Integrated disease management combines cultural, physical, biological, and chemical methods to control multiple pathogens simultaneously.
Watermelon cultivation is affected by several major fungal, bacterial, and viral diseases.
Chemical methods must be used judiciously to avoid pathogen resistance and environmental pollution.

diseases.disease_name: Charcoal rot Vine decline and fruit rot

general: Basal cankers observed in stem followed by girdling of the stem
Yellowing of foliage, wilting, and entire plant collapses
Initially brown lesions with amber colored droplets resembling gummy stem blight
Later lesions change to light tan color dotted with sclerotia
Large sunken areas with dark grey to black colour on fruits
early_symptoms: Brown lesions with amber colored droplets
advanced_symptoms: Light tan lesions with sclerotia and dark sunken areas on fruit
visual_field_symptoms: Basal cankers, stem girdling, yellowing, wilting, plant collapse

field_identification: Dark grey to black sunken areas on fruits

cultural_management: Crop rotation with non-host crop for 2 to 3 years
Irrigate thoroughly to avoid drought stress
Destroy infected plant residue
Grafting with susceptible scion to resistant rootstock

warnings_and_limitations: No chemical control measures have been reported to be effective.
research_findings: Grafting with susceptible scion to resistant rootstock is one of the effective methods for charcoal rot where chemical control is not useful.
